Based on this study, dose adjustment of artemether and lumefantrine tablets is considered unnecessary when co-administered with ketoconazole or other CYP3A4 inhibitors. However, due to the potential for increased lumefantrine concentrations, which could lead to QT prolongation, artemether and lumefantrine tablets should be used cautiously with other CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., antiretroviral drugs, macrolide antibiotics, antidepressants, imidazole antifungal agents). 8. Oral administration of mefloquine in 14 healthy volunteers (3 doses of 500 mg, 250 mg, and 250 mg) followed 12 hours later by artemether and lumefantrine tablets (6 doses of 4 tablets containing 20 mg artemether/120 mg lumefantrine per tablet) had no effect on plasma concentrations of artemether or the artemether/DHA ratio. However, there was a 30% reduction in Cmax and a 40% reduction in AUC of lumefantrine, possibly due to reduced absorption secondary to mefloquine-induced decreased bile production. 9. However, the mean AUC of artemether was 46% lower when administered with quinine compared to artemether and lumefantrine tablets alone. Nevertheless, quinine should be used cautiously in patients following treatment with artemether and lumefantrine tablets due to the long elimination half-life of lumefantrine and the potential for additive effects on the QT interval. However, artemether and lumefantrine tablets should be used cautiously in patients on antiretroviral drugs such as HIV protease inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, as decreased artemether, DHA, and/or lumefantrine concentrations may reduce the antimalarial efficacy of the tablets, and increased lumefantrine concentrations may cause QT prolongation. 13. No clinical drug-drug interaction studies between artemether and lumefantrine tablets and hormonal contraceptives have been performed. In vitro studies revealed that the metabolism of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel was not induced by artemether, DHA, or lumefantrine. However, artemether has been reported to weakly induce the activity of CYP2C19, CYP2B6, and CYP3A in humans. Therefore, co-administration of artemether and lumefantrine tablets may potentially reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. 14. In a healthy adult volunteer parallel-group study including a placebo and moxifloxacin control group (n=42 per group), administration of the 6-dose regimen of artemether and lumefantrine tablets was associated with QTcF (Fridericia) prolongation. Following administration of the 6-dose regimen (4 tablets per dose, totaling 80 mg artemether/480 mg lumefantrine per dose) taken with food, the maximum mean change from baseline and placebo-adjusted QTcF was 7.5 msec (1-sided 95% upper CI: 11 msec). There was a concentration-dependent increase in QTcF for lumefantrine. 15. In clinical trials conducted in children, no patient had a QTcF >500 msec. Over 5% of patients had an increase in QTcF of over 60 msec. 16. In clinical trials conducted in adults, QTcF prolongation >500 msec was reported in 3 patients (0.3%). Over 6% of adults had a QTcF increase of over 60 msec from baseline. 17. Carcinogenicity studies were not conducted. No evidence of mutagenicity was detected. The artemether-lumefantrine combination was evaluated using the Salmonella and Escherichia/mammalian-microsome mutagenicity test, the gene mutation test with Chinese hamster cells V79, the cytogenetic test on Chinese hamster cells in vitro, and the rat micronucleus test in vivo. 18. Pregnancy rates were reduced by about half in female rats dosed for 2 to 4 weeks with the artemether-lumefantrine combination at 1000 mg/kg (approximately 9 times the clinical dose based on body surface area comparisons). Male rats dosed for 70 days showed increases in abnormal sperm (87% abnormal) and increased testes weights at 30 mg/kg doses (approximately one-third the clinical dose). Higher doses (approximately 9 times the clinical dose) resulted in decreased sperm motility and 100% abnormal sperm cells. 19. Neonatal rats (7 to 21 days old) were more sensitive to the toxic effects of artemether (a component of artemether and lumefantrine tablets) than older juvenile rats or adults. Mortality and severe clinical signs were observed in neonatal rats at doses well tolerated in pups above 22 days old. 20. The efficacy of artemether and lumefantrine tablets was evaluated for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum in HIV-negative patients in 8 clinical studies. Uncomplicated malaria was defined as symptomatic P. falciparum malaria without signs and symptoms of severe malaria or evidence of vital organ dysfunction. Baseline parasite density ranged from 500/μL to 200,000/μL (0.01% to 4% parasitemia).
